summary: Wilhelm Scherer was a linguist who earned his PhD at the University of Vienna and studied under Moriz Haupt, Franz Bopp, Leopold von Ranke, and Karl Müllenhoff. He held professorships at Vienna, Strasbourg, and the University of Berlin.

Wilhelm Schmidt worked in linguistics and religious studies after studying at Berlin and Vienna. He served as director of the Anima Mundi Museum and Anthropos Institute, and taught at the University of Vienna and the University of Fribourg.

Wilhelm Schott specialized in Sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied at Giessen, Halle-Wittenberg (PhD), and Berlin, later serving as privatdozent at Halle and Berlin, and as apl. Professor in Berlin from 1838 to 1884.

Wilhelm Schulze, an Indologist and linguist, studied under Heymann Steinthal, Johannes Schmidt, and Heinrich Zimmer, earning a PhD at Greifswald. He held chairs at Göttingen and the University of Berlin, and taught at Greifswald and Marburg.

Wilhelm Siegling specialized in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied under Richard Pischel (earning his PhD at Berlin) and Emil Sieg, later working at Berlin's Ethnological Museum and the Prussian Academy of Sciences.

Wilhelm Solf studied Indology under Richard Pischel at Halle-Wittenberg, earning a PhD, and later obtained a Dr.iuris from Jena. He also studied under Albrecht Weber, Franz Kielhorn, and Friedrich Bechtel, and held a post at Kiel University.

Wilhelm Storck was a scholar in linguistics and other fields. He completed his PhD at Humboldt University of Berlin under Franz Bopp, also studying with Albrecht Weber and Moriz Haupt, and became an associate professor at the University of Münster.

Wilhelm Streitberg worked in linguistics and Indology, earning a doctorate at Leipzig under Karl Brugmann and August Leskien. He held professorships at the University of Fribourg, the University of Münster, and the University of Munich.

Wilhelm Tomaschek worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, history, archaeology, and linguistics. After studying at the University of Vienna under Friedrich Müller and Franz Xaver Miklosich, he served as professor of geography at Graz and Vienna.

Wilhelm Vatke was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He studied at Halle-Wittenberg, Göttingen, and Humboldt University of Berlin, where he later held an academic post from circa 1830 to 1882.

Wilhelm Volck, a scholar of religious studies, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, studied under Friedrich von Spiegel at Erlangen-Nuremberg. He held posts at Erlangen-Nuremberg, Tartu (ordinarius of Semitic Philology), Greifswald, and Rostock.

Wilhelm Wackernagel was a linguist who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin under Karl Lachmann and August Boeckh. He spent his career in Basel as a teacher at the Gymnasium am Münsterplatz and as an ordinarius professor at the university.

Wilhelm Wissmann was a linguist who studied under Wilhelm Schulze at Humboldt University of Berlin, where he completed his PhD and worked as an assistant. He later held professorships at Freiburg, Königsberg, and the University of Munich.

Wilhelm Wundt was a scholar of philosophy and other fields who studied at Tübingen, Heidelberg, and Berlin. He held academic posts at Heidelberg University, the University of Zurich, and the University of Leipzig.

Wilhelm von Humboldt worked in linguistics, Indology, and philosophy, studying under Georg Christoph Lichtenberg, Christian Gottlob Heyne, and Antoine-Léonard Chézy. He served as a Prussian minister and held a post at the Humboldt University of Berlin.
Wilhelm von Pochhammer was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed his studies at the universities of Freiburg, Marburg, Munich, and Bonn.
Will Sweetman is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who studied at Lancaster University and the University of Cambridge. He was appointed professor at the University of Otago circa 2003.

Will Tuladhar-Douglas works in religious and Buddhist studies. After studying at the University of Oxford and Wolfson College, he lectured at the University of Aberdeen, directed the Scottish Centre for Himalayan Research, and served as a research fellow at Hamburg.

Willard Gurdon Oxtoby was a religious and Iranian studies scholar educated at Stanford, Princeton, and Harvard. He taught at McGill and Yale before holding a long-term professorship and founding directorship at Trinity College and the University of Toronto.

Willard L. Johnson specialized in Indology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Oberlin College and the University of Wisconsin-Madison, he taught at California State University, Long Beach, Oberlin College, Del Mar College, and San Diego State University.
